title: Pending Home Sales Index (NAR, August 2026 data) — the contracts-signed read that predates the decision, 10:00 a.m. ET on FOMC+1 and September witching eve
source: IR: the publisher's own 2026 forward calendar — nar.realtor/newsroom/nar-statistical-news-release-schedule (302 -> /press-releases/..., HTTP 200, 483,177 bytes, re-fetched direct 2026-09-08 and byte-identical to the 2026-09-06 fetch) and its downloadable twin /sites/default/files/2025-11/2026-nar-statistical-news-release-schedule.docx (HTTP 200, 55,384 bytes, published 2025-11), whose 2026 table reads verbatim "Thu., Sep. 17 | August Pending Home Sales Index" under the standing note "All releases are distributed at 10 a.m. Eastern Time"; the same table puts "Thu., Sep. 10 | August Existing-Home Sales". Promoted from the `EST:` proposal filed 2026-09-08 by the fomc-2026-09-16 sweep, on the precedent pending-home-sales-2026-12-17 and existing-home-sales-2026-11-12 already set (NAR produces this series rather than reporting someone else's). PROMOTED ON EXECUTION, NOT ONLY ON SCHEDULE, and on twice the evidence the 12-17 lane had: NAR's own newsroom <time> elements score the 2026 schedule 2 for 2 to the exact day and the exact hour — June data scheduled "Thu., July 16" published 2026-07-16T09:00:00-05:00, July data scheduled "Tue., Aug. 18" published 2026-08-18T09:01:00-05:00 (both 10:00/10:01 ET). ONE CONFLICTING NAR SURFACE, RECORDED NOT HIDDEN: the pending-home-sales statistics page (HTTP 200, 565,653 bytes, also byte-identical to 2026-09-06) still reads "Pending Home Sales for August 2026 will be released on Thursday, September 10, 2026 at 10 a.m. Eastern" — uncorrected at D-9. That note is a SERIES-LABELLING error rather than a competing schedule: 09-10 is the schedule's and the .docx's own August EXISTING-home sales row, and the same page carries the day-20 release cadence NAR abandoned in January 2026. The resolution is registered as FT-pending-home-sales-2026-09-17-1, scored 2026-09-17. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: The August edition of the series whose December edition this calendar already tracks (pending-home-sales-2026-12-17). PHSI counts contracts SIGNED, so the August data released here predates the 09-16 FOMC decision entirely and can contain no reaction to it — the conflation risk 09-17 carries, one session after a decision priced a coin flip. THREE FINDINGS FROM THIS EVENT'S INITIAL RESEARCH (2026-09-08, D-9), two of which narrow an inheritance rather than widen it. (1) THE 12-17 LANE'S WIDE-SESSION EXPECTATION DOES NOT TRANSFER. That ledger's opex-eve widening is a DECEMBER result (ITB median session range 2.691% vs 1.830%, n=12, p=0.008); measured today on the same metric, SEPTEMBER opex eve is null on all three instruments — ITB 1.852% vs an 1.828% baseline (n=12, p=0.922), XHB 1.588% vs 1.613% (p=0.917), SPY 0.923% vs 0.874% (p=0.805), 2014+. This agrees with the same-day housing-starts-2026-09-17 ledger, which found opex eve null (p=0.94) on its own gap metric. (2) FOMC+1 IS THE REAL WIDENER, AND ONLY IN RANGE. On 94 FOMC+1 sessions 2014+, ITB's median session range is 2.094% vs 1.828% (p=0.012; ex-2020 n=87, 2.091% vs 1.798%, p=0.004) and XHB 1.979% vs 1.613% (p=0.001), while |open->close| is null everywhere (ITB p=0.634, XHB p=0.132, SPY p=0.201) — wide, not directional. BUT the exact 2026 geometry, a September witching eve that is ALSO FOMC+1, has occurred five times (2014-09-18, 2019-09-19, 2020-09-17, 2024-09-19, 2025-09-18) and did NOT widen: ITB median 1.581% (p=0.550), XHB 1.630% (p=0.962), SPY 0.698% (p=0.532), and all five ITB sessions came in under the 2.504% baseline p75. Registered as FT-pending-home-sales-2026-09-17-3. (3) THE BUILDER COLLISION FIRES ON THE DECEMBER SLOT, NOT THIS ONE. Re-run EDGAR 8-K Item 2.02 dates (caches busted 2026-09-08) show only LEN and KBH of the six tracked builders ever file in September; KBH's FY2026 lag (Q1 +24d, Q2 +23d) puts its Q3 at ~09-23/24, after the print, and LEN's FY2026 lag COMPRESSED to +12d/+11d from FY2025's +20d/+17d/+19d, pointing at ~09-11/09-12 — before it. Registered as FT-pending-home-sales-2026-09-17-2. Impact stays `low` and `symbols: []`: no house playbook is macro- or housing-keyed, no instrument attaches, and `confirmed` licenses nothing.
